SOURCE: ABC News live updates, 22 Nov 2026 (curl extraction)

Talks between the U.S. and Iran remain stalled despite the two countries signing a memorandum of understanding in June, aimed at ending the war that began with joint American-Israeli strikes on the country in February. The opening strikes killed a host of top Iranian officials and commanders, among them Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei.

The two sides have continued to exchange strikes, though have not returned to the intense fighting seen in the early stages of the conflict. The U.S. says it is enforcing a naval blockade of the country's Persian Gulf and Gulf of Oman ports, while Iran claims control over the strategic Strait of Hormuz and continues to claim attacks on shipping transiting the waterway.

Meanwhile, intensified fighting between Saudi-backed Yemeni forces and Iran-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen has seen the latter repeatedly attack Saudi military, oil infrastructure and transport facilities.

See the most recent developments below.

UKMTO reports incident 'involving tanker and military forces' in Gulf of OmanU.K. Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) says they have received a report of an incident "involving a tanker and military forces in the Gulf of Oman."

Authorities are aware of the incident and investigations are ongoing, the UKMTO said.

Separately, the IRGC navy, per official Iranian state media, say two tankers have "exploded and stopped due to collision with sea mines north of Ghanem Island and east of the Strait of Hormuz."

The IRGC navy claims the tankers were passing through "unauthorized routes" and did not comply with instructions.

It is not confirmed whether these two incidents are the same.

Regional nations condemn Iranian attack on BahrainSaudi Arabia, Kuwait and Qatar issued statements on Sunday condemning Iran's attack on Bahrain on Saturday, which Manama said injured two people and caused a file at a civilian industrial facility.

Qatar's Foreign Ministry said the attack constituted a "flagrant violation of its sovereignty and territorial integrity, and a blatant breach of international law, the United Nations Charter, and the principles of good neighborliness."

The Saudi Foreign Ministry described the attack as "heinous" and said it holds Iran responsible for the consequences of its continued perpetration of these flagrant attacks."

Kuwait's Foreign Ministry said that Iranian attacks on Bahrain "threaten the region's security and stability."

Flames rise as fire breaks out at a civilian facility, following what Bahrain says was an Iranian attack, in Sitra, Bahrain, on Nov. 21, 2026, in this still image obtained from a social media video.Social Media via Reuters5:42 AM ESTIRGC claims shooting down of US droneIran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps on Sunday claimed to have shot down a U.S. MQ-1 Predator drone east of the Strait of Hormuz.

The IRGC made its claim in a statement carried by the state-run IRNA News Agency. U.S. Central Command did not immediately comment on the IRGC claim.

Saudi Arabia intercepts Houthi drone targeting Riyadh, spokesperson saysSaudi forces intercepted a drone launched by the Iran-backed Houthis in Yemen toward the Saudi capital Riyadh on Sunday, military spokesperson Col. Turki Al-Maliki said in a post to X.
